BXL-2425-00003-v5.headline: Demand that the government keep paying out the "Rénolution" home-renovation premiums without interruption, after the scheme ran out of money and froze new applications.
BXL-2425-00003-v5.proposed_by: MR, PS and Vooruit members (Czekalski, Emmery, De Beukelaer, Godfrin, Vainsel, Laarissi, Belguenani, Smet)
BXL-2425-00003-v5.source_brief:
Brussels pays "Rénolution" premiums to help residents insulate and renovate their homes, but the pot ran dry and the Region stopped processing new applications, leaving households who had already done the work waiting to be paid. This resolution is a formal instruction to the government to guarantee those payments continue.

- **A demand, not a cheque.** A resolution carries no budget of its own; it asks the government to find the money and resume processing the backlog of premium claims.
- **Who it touches.** The premiums are meant to make insulation and renovation affordable for ordinary households in an ageing, energy-hungry housing stock, not just owners who can front the cost.
- **Amended on the floor.** Two extra demands were proposed for the operative part of the text.
- **The rub:** almost no one argues against paying people who already renovated in good faith, so the real question is whether a resolution with no funding attached changes anything, or just records Parliament's wish while the caretaker government decides.
deep_facts: The text is the "proposition de résolution relative à la continuité du versement des primes « Rénolution »" (A-9), tabled by Aurélie Czekalski, Isabelle Emmery, Christophe De Beukelaer, Aline Godfrin, Cécile Vainsel, Mounir Laarissi, Imane Belguenani and Pascal Smet (CRI, 4 Oct 2024).

A resolution is a non-binding instruction from Parliament to the government; it does not itself open or release credits, but formally requests action on the continued payment of the Rénolution renovation/energy premiums (CRI, 4 Oct 2024).
Two amendments to the operative part ("dispositif") were tabled: amendment no. 1 on the third indent ("tiret 3") and amendment no. 2 on the fourth indent ("tiret 4") (CRI, 4 Oct 2024).

Context from the same legislature: the Rénolution premium scheme suspended processing of new applications on 16 August 2024 for lack of budget, leaving households unable to be paid for works already carried out, before additional credits were later released (CRI, 19 Dec 2024).
Roughly 60% of Brussels housing dates from before 1970 and is often old and energy-inefficient, the renovation of which the premiums are intended to support (CRI, 19 Dec 2024).
BXL-2425-00003-v5.deep_lectura:
**Analyst read** *(inference — not stated verbatim in the record)*
- A resolution is the cheapest possible lever: it commits no money and binds no one, so the substantive choice is whether Parliament should put pressure on a caretaker government that has no full budget to act with, or wait for the incoming majority.
- Tabling it days before communal elections, with sponsors drawn from several parties, reads as a cross-party signal to anxious renovating households that the premiums will not be abandoned.
- The two amendments to specific indents suggest a fight over exactly what the government is being asked to commit to, and over how far the finer obligations should reach.
- A 'no' here is less opposition to the premiums than a statement that resolutions without funding are empty gestures.
BXL-2425-00003-v5.raw_fr: Proposition de résolution relative à la continuité du versement des primes « Rénolution » (A-9). Le texte demande au gouvernement d'assurer la poursuite du paiement de ces primes de rénovation. Deux amendements au dispositif, portant sur le tiret 3 et le tiret 4, ont été déposés.

BXL-2425-00003-v10.headline: Postpone the next phase of the Low Emission Zone by two years, pushing the planned 1 January 2025 ban on Euro 5 diesel and Euro 2 petrol cars back to 1 January 2027.
BXL-2425-00003-v10.proposed_by: MR, PS and Vooruit members (d'Ursel, Ikazban, Laarissi, Weytsman, Dönmez, Bennani, Belguenani, Agic, Diallo, Willocx)
BXL-2425-00003-v10.source_brief:
Brussels' Low Emission Zone tightens step by step, banning ever-older, more polluting cars from the city. The next tightening was scheduled to take effect on 1 January 2025 and would have shut out Euro 5 diesel and Euro 2 petrol vehicles. This ordinance pushes that deadline back two years, to 1 January 2027.

- **What changes.** Cars that were due to be banned in weeks get a two-year reprieve to keep entering the zone.
- **The social case.** Owners of these vehicles, often lower-income drivers and small tradespeople, are told they were facing the cost of scrapping a working car or buying a new one on short notice.
- **The health case.** The vehicles targeted by the delayed phase are described as responsible for 40% of nitrogen-oxide emissions while making up a small share of the fleet; air quality breaches EU and WHO norms across most of the city.
- **The rub:** the choice is whether to spare tens of thousands of car owners a costly switch right now, or hold the line on a seven-year-old, publicly announced clean-air calendar that doctors and environmental groups say is already overdue.
deep_facts: The text is the "proposition d'ordonnance visant à fixer la mise en œuvre de la prochaine phase de la zone de basses émissions (LEZ) au 1er janvier 2027" (A-10), tabled by Anne-Charlotte d'Ursel, Jamal Ikazban, Mounir Laarissi, David Weytsman, Ibrahim Dönmez, Sofia Bennani, Imane Belguenani, Leila Agic, Elhadj Moussa Diallo and Olivier Willocx (CRI, 4 Oct 2024).
The next LEZ phase was due to enter into force on 1 January 2025; the ordinance sets its implementation date at 1 January 2027 instead, a two-year postponement (CRI, 4 Oct 2024).

The vehicles concerned by the delayed phase are Euro 5 diesel and Euro 2 (and older) petrol cars; Euro 5 diesels are described as the vehicles at the centre of the dieselgate scandal, able to pollute as much as Euro 3 diesels already banned for five years (CRI, 4 Oct 2024).
These vehicles were stated to make up 9.3% of the fleet while causing 40% of nitrogen-oxide (NOx) emissions (CRI, 4 Oct 2024).
On the current (un-delayed) schedule, diesel cars could still enter the Region for six more years and petrol cars for eleven more years (CRI, 4 Oct 2024).

Air-quality figures cited: since the LEZ was introduced, Brussels air quality improved by 30–40%, more so in disadvantaged areas; 98% of the population lives where air fails the WHO norm of 10 µg/m³; the EU PM norm of 40 µg/m³ is exceeded at four sites, and the future EU norm of 20 µg/m³ would be missed at nine of thirteen measuring stations (CRI, 4 Oct 2024).

Health context cited: respiratory problems are among the most common reasons for doctor visits and sick leave in Brussels; some 200,000 residents have respiratory problems and 80,000 suffer from asthma; life expectancy is markedly lower in Saint-Josse-ten-Noode than in Woluwe-Saint-Pierre (CRI, 4 Oct 2024).

Existing accompanying measures were referenced: the Bruxell'air premium of more than 1,000 euros; the LEZ premium of up to 16,000 euros for professionals with a utility vehicle; retrofit support to replace a combustion engine with an electric one; electric-vehicle leasing; charging-point installation; and existing derogations for persons with reduced mobility and school transport of disabled children (CRI, 4 Oct 2024).

Three amendments to Article 2 were tabled: amendment no. 1 (de Patoul) widening derogations on socio-economic grounds, for low-mileage vehicles under 3,000 km/year and for holders of a medical certificate; amendment no. 2 (Rittweger de Moor / Michaux Maimone) granting Euro 5+ diesel and Euro 2+ petrol vehicles automatic, free LEZ access until 31 December 2034; and amendment no. 3 extending the same postponement to taxi-sector vehicles (CRI, 4 Oct 2024).
Once adopted, the ordinance is submitted to the government for sanction (CRI, 4 Oct 2024).

The proposal was debated jointly with three other ordinance texts on the LEZ (A-11 De Smedt establishing a moratorium on the LEZ phases; A-12 Smet/Mouani postponing the access restriction; A-13 Ahidar postponing the restriction on Euro 5 / Euro V diesel vehicles) (CRI, 4 Oct 2024).
BXL-2425-00003-v10.deep_lectura:
**Analyst read** *(inference — not stated verbatim in the record)*
- The vote pits an immediate, concrete cost on a defined group of car owners against a diffuse, statistical health benefit for the whole population, the classic shape of a clean-air fight, sharpened by being decided weeks before communal elections.
- Changing a seven-year-old calendar three months before it bites is framed by opponents as a governance problem in itself: people who already scrapped or replaced compliant-by-2025 cars get no reprieve, while those who waited are rewarded.
- The amendments map the alternatives on the table: a narrow social carve-out, a near-total exemption to 2034, and a taxi-specific delay, set against a clean two-year slip for everyone rather than targeted relief.
- Joining four competing texts into one debate frames a choice between the mildest option (a fixed two-year delay), a full moratorium and the status quo.
BXL-2425-00003-v10.raw_fr: Proposition d'ordonnance visant à fixer la mise en œuvre de la prochaine phase de la zone de basses émissions (LEZ) au 1er janvier 2027 (A-10). La prochaine étape, qui devait entrer en vigueur le 1er janvier 2025 et viser les véhicules diesel Euro 5 et essence Euro 2, est ainsi reportée de deux ans. Trois amendements à l'article 2, élargissant les dérogations ou prolongeant l'accès de certains véhicules, ont été déposés.
